text:
alex: Hey team — FinEdge POC needs a tight egress allowlist for the Private deployment. They are evaluating two connectivity patterns: VPC peering (TGW) vs interface PrivateLink backed by an internal NLB. Requirements: static IPs or small IP ranges for firewall whitelist, client IP preserved for logs, and compatibility with their TLS-inspecting perimeter (they terminate TLS in a proxy). Can we give a short presales answer + sample iptables/snippet they can paste?

maria: Quick clarifying Qs: which cloud/region? is this Redwood Private (customer VPC + control plane managed) or Dedicated hosting from us? Also do they require mutual TLS to the inference endpoints?

alex: AWS us-east-2 for the POC. It's Redwood Private (we deploy control plane into their VPCs). No mTLS requested now, they use token auth but want client IP for audit correlation.

samir: TL;DR first: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) does NOT give you a stable public IP range you can whitelist because ENIs are in subnets and IPs can change; source IP preservation depends on the path. Options sorted by whitelistability: 
1) Fixed Egress EIP via NAT/Proxy (recommended) — you own static EIP(s) on a NAT GW or outbound proxy in your network; whitelist those EIP(s) on your firewall; source IP will be NATed to that EIP (so you lose original client IP unless you forward X-Forwarded-For from the proxy).
2) VPC Peering/TGW — traffic stays inside AWS and preserves original source IP across peering/TGW; problem: peered VPC ENIs still change and you cannot provide a single stable external IP to on-prem firewall; works well if there is no on-prem firewall white-listing requirement (or if you peer to their AWS account).
3) PrivateLink (interface endpoints + internal NLB) — connection is via interface endpoints. Source IP seen by the service will be the node/private ENI IP (not original public client IP) unless you enable proxy protocol on NLB + application understands it. Not suitable if the customer's TLS inspector breaks SNI/ProxyProtocol.

samir: Sample short guidance for FinEdge: 
- If they need a single static IP range to add to corporate perimeter, we recommend an outbound NAT/proxy with an Elastic IP (NAT GW or outbound proxy) in their account and route Redwood Private traffic through it. That lets them whitelist 1–3 EIP(s).
- If they need original client IP in our service logs: deploy a small HTTP(S) proxy (nginx/Envoy) in their VPC that forwards X-Forwarded-For and routes to the Redwood endpoint. For TCP/TLS termination by their perimeter, you need to preserve TLS (no MITM) or use mTLS on the internal channel.

samir: Example iptables snippet they can paste on an outbound proxy VM (assume proxy handles TLS):
```
# permit outbound to Redwood NAT target (replace X.Y.Z.0/28 with your EIP block)
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d X.Y.Z.0/28 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# allow return
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
# drop everything else to force proxying
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP
```

samir: If they prefer TGW/peering and want client IPs preserved, note that traffic keeps private IPs; the tradeoff is you can't give them a single external IP to put in on-prem firewall unless you NAT out through a dedicated EIP.

jen: On the PrivateLink note — interface endpoints use AWS-managed IPs. If their firewall requires allowlist by remote IP, PrivateLink won't help. Also if their TLS inspector terminates TLS and re-mints certs, we recommend a no-inspect path or a mutual TLS hop between their proxy and Redwood (we can configure that for Private deployments, requires ops setup).

alex: They also asked about port list. Can we provide a minimal set?

samir: Minimal ports for outbound to Redwood Private endpoints (typical):
- TCP 443 (HTTPS) — main inference/control plane traffic
- TCP 53 (DNS) or allow egress to their DNS resolver
- ICMP allowed for monitoring (optional)
If they use gRPC over TLS it's still 443. For websockets/streams we still use 443.

maria: Pricing question came up: are there extra costs for static EIPs / NAT GW if we recommend NAT egress? We'll need to call this out in the POC TCO.

samir: Yes, NAT GW + EIP + transfer costs are billed by cloud provider — we should surface an estimate in the POC doc. Redwood Dedicated can also be set up with our outbound EIP pool for an additional configuration fee (I will confirm exact pricing with infra).

ops-bot: Deployment note: POC control plane for FinEdge queued — infra ticket #INF-11234 created (assigned to samir).

alex: One last security question from their SecOps: can Redwood rotate certs/keys without breaking the POC?

samir: For Private deployments we support rolling cert updates; we schedule a short maintenance window. If they require zero-downtime cert rotation, we can coordinate a canary + handshake test.

maria: Action items: 
- Samir: provide a short one-pager with (A) NAT/EIP approach + sample allowlist, (B) TGW/peering notes and client-IP tradeoffs, (C) minimal ports.
- Samir: estimate infra cost delta for NAT GW vs no-NAT.
- Alex: share this thread with FinEdge and ask for proxy/NAT preference.

samir: Will do — I'll drop the one-pager and a tiny diagram into the customer handoff doc today.

alex: Thanks — will update FinEdge and loop back. :thumbsup:
